name: Question 9
problem:
If the following system of differential equations is written in the form ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),$ then what is the matrix $A?$

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)-2{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)=0 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)+5{x}_{1}(t)-9{x}_{2}(t)=0\end{aligned}
$$
worked_solution:
A first-order linear system of differential equations with two dependent variables is a system of equations that takes the following standard form:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=a(t){x}_{1}(t)+b(t){x}_{2}(t)+f(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=c(t){x}_{1}(t)+d(t){x}_{2}(t)+g(t)\end{aligned}
$$

where

- $a(t),$ $b(t),$ $c(t),$ $d(t),$ $f(t),$ and $g(t)$ are known functions, and

- ${x}_{1}(t)$ and ${x}_{2}(t)$ are unknown functions (dependent variables).

Such a system can always be written in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)
$$

where

$$
x(t)=[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}(t) \\ {x}_{2}(t)\end{aligned}],\,A=[\begin{aligned}a(t) & b(t) \\ c(t) & d(t)\end{aligned}],\,f(t)=[\begin{aligned}f(t) \\ g(t)\end{aligned}].
$$

We have the following system.

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)-2{x}_{1}(t)+{x}_{2}(t)=0 \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)+5{x}_{1}(t)-9{x}_{2}(t)=0\end{aligned}
$$

Writing our system in standard form, we get the following:

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}^{′}(t)=2{x}_{1}(t)-{x}_{2}(t) \\ {x}_{2}^{′}(t)=-5{x}_{1}(t)+9{x}_{2}(t).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can rewrite our system in matrix form as follows:

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -5 & 9\end{aligned}]x(t)
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ -5 & 9\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 9

If the following system of differential equations is written in the form x′(t)=Ax(t), then what is the matrix A? {x1′(t)−2x1(t)+x2(t)=0x2′(t)+5x1(t)−9x2(t)=0

a
A=[2−1−59]
b
A=[−215−9]
c
A=[−1−295]
d
A=[2−5−19]
e
A=[−251−9]
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A first-order linear system of differential equations with two dependent variables is a system of equations that takes the following standard form: {x1′(t)=a(t)x1(t)+b(t)x2(t)+f(t)x2′(t)=c(t)x1(t)+d(t)x2(t)+g(t) where

  • a(t), b(t), c(t), d(t), f(t), and g(t) are known functions, and

  • x1(t) and x2(t) are unknown functions (dependent variables).

Such a system can always be written in the form x′(t)=Ax(t)+f(t)

where x(t)=[x1(t)x2(t)],A=[a(t)b(t)c(t)d(t)],f(t)=[f(t)g(t)].

We have the following system.

{x1′(t)−2x1(t)+x2(t)=0x2′(t)+5x1(t)−9x2(t)=0

Writing our system in standard form, we get the following:

{x1′(t)=2x1(t)−x2(t)x2′(t)=−5x1(t)+9x2(t).

So, we can rewrite our system in matrix form as follows:

x′(t)=[2−1−59]x(t)

Therefore, we have

A=[2−1−59].
